evidence.why: Initialization, assertion and final guarded call.
Position/history updates and exact state transitions.

facts.rationale: Corrects the debug interpretation and preserves the distinction between Enabled and other non-disabled capsule states.
facts.value: If the selected capsule is disabled or its stored group differs from the command group, the handler assigns the group, sets HitCapsule_Enabled, sets xDC8_word.flags.x16, clears xDAA_flag.b2 and initializes collision state. Other non-disabled same-group capsules retain their existing state during this initialization step while their properties are refreshed. A nonzero attachment bone requires the dynamic bone table and reports an assertion when it is absent. After decoding, the handler clears x43_b2 and calls it_8027129C only when HSD_GObj_804D7838 is non-null and its s_link exceeds 11. That helper updates position/history and transitions Enabled to Unk2 or Unk2 to Unk3; Unk3 updates history, while Disabled and Unk4 return without those updates. This branch is not debug registration.

evidence.why: Promotion, operand decoding and path-dependent width.

facts.rationale: The packed selector is unsigned despite the signed local variable and redundant nonnegative test.
facts.value: An ItCmd-compatible callback with signature void(Item_GObj*, CommandInfo*). Its initial word contains an unsigned eight-bit behavior selector in itAnimlistCmdUnk.opcode, promoted to s32 for dispatch. Selectors 0–2 use the next two words for a 32-bit SFX identifier and two u8 audio controls. Selectors 10–11 consume the same three-word width but ignore those operands. Other selectors perform no audio operation and consume two words.

evidence.why: Ordering helper and actual effect scale literal.
Hitbox scaling and reciprocal model-scale argument.

facts.rationale: Preserves demonstrated numeric flow without claiming exact 1/256 arithmetic or unobserved compiled conversion behavior.
facts.value: Source-level numeric consumers multiply packed effect coordinates and hitbox size/offset fields by 0.003906f, approximately 1/256. Hitbox creation and scale updates pass 1.0f / item->scl to the scale-adjustment helper. The main interpreter uses 0.0f as its due-time threshold and F32_MAX as a special animation-relative timer sentinel. The MUST_MATCH ordering helper also lists two 2^52-based double literals, but this source does not establish their emitted placement or compiler-generated conversion consumers.

facts.rationale: Replaces an unsupported 40-byte compiled-layout assertion with the exact source evidence.
facts.value: The source's MUST_MATCH-only sdata2_order helper lists, in source order, float literal 0.00390599994f, double literals 4503599627370496.0 and 4503601774854144.0, and float literals 1.0f, 0.0f and 3.40282347e+38f. These source expressions do not establish a compiled section's byte extent, alignment, padding or emitted literal order.

evidence.why: Geometry scale and reciprocal model adjustment.

facts.rationale: Separates supported numeric roles from unsupported emitted literal-pool claims.
facts.value: The associated source numeric constants support packed-geometry scaling, reciprocal item-model scale adjustment, due-time comparison and the F32_MAX command-timer sentinel. A MUST_MATCH helper records additional double literals and an intended literal ordering; compiled pool placement and conversion-bias use remain unverified without compiled evidence.

evidence.why: Complete reads and five cursor increments.

facts.value: A void ItCmd callback with signature void(Item_GObj*, CommandInfo*). It consumes five command words total: the initial selector word, one effect-ID/scalar word and three words containing six signed 16-bit vector components. Five cursor increments leave cmd->u at the next event; there are four continuation words, not five.

facts.rationale: Corrects the inherited continuation-word count without changing the transparent-adapter interpretation.
facts.value: Receives an Item_GObj and mutable CommandInfo from the secondary dispatcher and forwards both unchanged to it_80278F2C. The delegated decoder consumes five total words—the initial word plus four continuation words—extracting a joint selector, effect ID, scalar, base-offset vector and spread vector before calling it_80278800. The adapter itself performs no additional cursor movement.

evidence.why: Packed operands, arithmetic, mode and cursor progression.
Random displacement helper and effect-specific exceptions.

facts.rationale: Preserves decoding while making approximate arithmetic and exceptional effect branches explicit.
facts.value: Reads a ten-bit selector from the initial word, an effect ID and unsigned scalar from the next word, then six signed 16-bit components from three further words. Components are multiplied by 0.003906f into base-offset and spread vectors. It forwards these values to it_80278800 with mode 0 and leaves the cursor five words ahead. Downstream behavior depends on the effect ID: special branches may ignore spread or spawn synchronously even with mode 0; the default placement path adds centered random per-axis displacement and transforms through the selected item joint before further effect dispatch.

evidence.why: Main guards, dispatch and overlay adapters.
Overlay-backed context forwarded to owner callback.

facts.rationale: Corrects unconditional timer-reduction wording and preserves the two distinct mutable command contexts.
facts.value: Each main-interpreter invocation copies the item's cached animation frame into x524_cmd.frame_count and clears xDBC_itcmd_var4_word. A null command cursor returns before timer subtraction; otherwise only a timer unequal to F32_MAX is reduced by animation speed. The loop rechecks stream and timing guards, offers each due opcode to Command_Execute, and dispatches unconsumed opcodes through it_803F22A8[opcode - 10]. Handlers decode payload words, advance the shared cursor and mutate or forward item subsystem state. The separate overlay path supplies an overlay-backed command context to its own two-entry item adapter table.

evidence.why: Reset followed by one cursor increment.
Countdown use, fixed reset and separate priority lookup.

facts.rationale: Corrects the conflation of countdown and priority while retaining unconditional one-word reset behavior.
facts.value: Once dispatched, the handler unconditionally resets the item's overlay through it_80279BBC and advances exactly one command word. Reset nulls x8_ptr1 and x28_colanim.ptr, zeroes the completion countdown x4_pri and disables both blend channels. These fixed writes are idempotent. x4_pri is not the profile-table priority, and the reset does not write the profile table.

evidence.why: Countdown, reset fields and table priority comparison.

facts.rationale: Corrects the semantic interpretation of x4_pri without changing the supported reset behavior.
facts.value: Every invocation unconditionally resets the embedded overlay by nulling x8_ptr1 and x28_colanim.ptr, zeroing the completion countdown x4_pri and disabling both blend channels. It has no local timer, priority or active-overlay guard. Repeated calls leave those reset fields unchanged; it does not zero or otherwise modify profile-table priority values.

facts.rationale: Corrects countdown-versus-priority terminology and keeps caller-owned timing distinct.
facts.value: Every invocation unconditionally resets the embedded overlay by nulling x8_ptr1 and x28_colanim.ptr, zeroing the completion countdown x4_pri and disabling both blend channels. The wrapper contains no identifier, timer, priority or active-overlay guard; caller-side conditions determine when it runs. Repeated calls are idempotent for the reset fields. Profile-table priority values are not modified.

facts.rationale: Preserves both construction reset sites while correcting the claimed final construction state and countdown terminology.
facts.value: Establishes an inactive baseline for the item's embedded color-overlay controller by clearing its command source, color-animation reference, completion countdown and blend enables. Shared construction invokes it during baseline Item-record initialization and again during post-model spawn setup. This does not guarantee an inactive overlay at constructor return: later construction logic for hold kinds 0 and 6 can intentionally request profile 3.
